weeks.title: Foundations: Java for DSA, Complexity, Math, Bits, Arrays
weeks.resources: KK (Java basics → complexity lectures), Striver A2Z Step 1 (basics, maths, hashing intro), LC Explore Arrays 101
keyConcepts: Java toolkit: `int[]`, `ArrayList`, `HashMap`/`HashSet`, `Arrays.sort`/`Arrays.fill`, `Collections`, `StringBuilder`, `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, `long` overflow, and how a `Comparator` lambda works
Big-O for loops, nested loops, `log n` halving, and recursion (the recursion-tree idea); space complexity; best, average, and worst case
Maths: digit extraction, GCD (Euclid), primes and the Sieve of Eratosthenes, fast exponentiation
Bits: `&`, `|`, `^`, `~`, `<<`, `>>`, `>>>`; checking, setting, and clearing a bit; `n & (n-1)`
Arrays: traversal, in-place modification, reversal, rotation, and the matrix-as-2D-array view
weeks.milestone: You can write clean Java with collections, and you can state the time/space complexity of any loop-based code.

weeks.title: Arrays II: Two Pointers, Prefix Sum, Kadane, Intervals
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z Step 3 (arrays easy → hard), NC Two Pointers + Arrays & Hashing videos
keyConcepts: prefix sums plus a HashMap of seen prefixes
weeks.milestone: You can recognise when a problem needs two pointers, a prefix sum, or Kadane's algorithm, and you have solved your first Hard problem (with help is fine).

weeks.title: Hashing, Strings, Sliding Window
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z (strings + sliding window section), AV Sliding Window playlist, NC Sliding Window
keyConcepts: `StringBuilder` vs string concatenation (why `+` in a loop is O(n²))
the "at most K" minus "at most K-1" trick
weeks.milestone: You can write a variable sliding window template from memory and solve most string Mediums in 30 minutes.

weeks.title: Sorting + Binary Search
weeks.resources: AB (merge sort, quick sort), Striver A2Z Step 2 (sorting) + Step 4 (binary search), AV Binary Search playlist, LC Explore Binary Search
keyConcepts: bubble/selection/insertion sort (know them, never use them)
binary search invariants (`lo <= hi` vs `lo < hi`, and `mid = lo + (hi-lo)/2`)
binary search on the answer (monotonic predicate)
weeks.milestone: You can spot a monotonic predicate and apply binary search on the answer. You know merge sort's O(n log n) proof.

weeks.title: Recursion + Backtracking
weeks.resources: KK (recursion series, the best for beginners), Striver A2Z Step 6 (recursion), AV Recursion playlist
keyConcepts: base case, recursive call, and how the call stack works
deduplication by sorting first and skipping repeated values
weeks.milestone: You can write the subsets, permutations, and combination-sum templates from memory and draw their recursion trees.

weeks.title: Linked Lists
weeks.resources: KK (linked list lectures), Striver A2Z Step 7, LC Explore Linked List
keyConcepts: implementing singly and doubly linked lists
fast/slow pointers (finding the middle, Floyd's cycle detection and cycle start)
reversing a sub-list and reversing in k-groups
HashMap + doubly linked list for LRU
weeks.milestone: You can implement LRU Cache from scratch in under 30 minutes and reverse any segment of a list without bugs.

weeks.title: Stacks, Queues, Monotonic Stack, Deque
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z Step 9, AV Stack playlist (monotonic stack), LC Explore Queue & Stack
keyConcepts: `ArrayDeque` as both stack and queue (never use `Stack`)
monotonic stack (next greater/smaller element, previous smaller element)
monotonic deque for sliding window max
weeks.milestone: When you see "next greater" or "previous smaller" in a problem, you think monotonic stack immediately.

weeks.title: Binary Trees
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z Step 13 (the tree series is excellent), KK (trees), LC Explore Binary Tree, VisuAlgo
keyConcepts: BFS level order with a queue
height/depth computed bottom-up with return values
the "global answer + return a different value" pattern (diameter, max path sum)
converting a tree to a graph (parent map)
weeks.milestone: You can solve 80% of tree Mediums with "what does my recursive call return?" thinking.

weeks.title: BST, Heaps / Priority Queue, Tries
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z Steps 14 (BST), 17 (heaps), and 16 (tries) · AV Heap playlist · `TreeMap`/`TreeSet` docs (`floorKey`, `ceilingKey`)
keyConcepts: top-K problems using a heap of size K
weeks.milestone: You can pick the right tool among `PriorityQueue`, `TreeMap`, and a trie. You can explain the O(n log k) cost of the top-K approach.

weeks.title: Graphs I: Traversal, Grids, Cycles, Topological Sort
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z Step 15 (graph series, the best free graph course), WF (graph theory playlist), NC Graphs
keyConcepts: BFS/DFS on graphs and grids (4-direction arrays)
cycle detection in undirected graphs (parent tracking) and directed graphs (DFS colouring)
BFS shortest path on unweighted graphs
weeks.milestone: You can turn a word problem into a graph (nodes = ?, edges = ?) and choose between BFS, DFS, and topological sort.

weeks.title: Graphs II (Shortest Paths, DSU, MST, Bridges) + Greedy
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z Step 15 (second half), AB (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, Prim, Kruskal), WF (Union-Find, Tarjan), Striver A2Z Step 12 (greedy)
keyConcepts: Dijkstra with a `PriorityQueue` (and why it fails with negative edges)
Union-Find with path compression and union by rank
greedy: the exchange argument, sorting by end time, "why does greedy work here?"
weeks.milestone: You can write Dijkstra and DSU from memory in under 10 minutes each, and you can justify a greedy choice instead of guessing.

weeks.title: Dynamic Programming I
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z Step 16 (the DP series is excellent), AV Dynamic Programming playlist (knapsack and LCS families), NC 1-D DP / 2-D DP
keyConcepts: recursion → memoisation → tabulation → space optimisation (do all four for the first 10 problems)
weeks.milestone: For any DP problem you can write the state, transition, and base case in words before you code.

weeks.title: DP II + Advanced (Segment Tree, Fenwick Tree, KMP)
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z Step 16 (second half), AV (Matrix Chain Multiplication playlist), WF (segment tree, Fenwick tree), CPA (prefix function / KMP)
keyConcepts: LIS in O(n²) and in O(n log n) with binary search
stock problems as a state machine
weeks.milestone: ~300+ problems solved across every core topic. You have a personal template file for each pattern.

weeks.title: Week 1: Two apps, one repo
weeks.objective: Set up the monorepo with a layered .NET solution and a Vite React + TypeScript app, and make them talk to each other.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Skeleton" merged: /api solution with 4 layers, /web Vite app, the web page shows the API's health status, both build in CI-ready scripts.

weeks.title: Week 2: The job-search domain in C# and TypeScript
weeks.objective: Model applications, companies and interviews in modern C# with rules and tests, mirror them as TypeScript types, and render them with components.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Domain model" merged: domain entities with guarded status transitions and xUnit tests (80% on Domain); TS types and a static list rendered from components.

weeks.title: Week 3: First real feature: the applications list
weeks.objective: Serve applications from the API through DI and DTOs, and show them in React with loading and error states.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Applications list" merged: GET /api/applications (in-memory store behind an interface) and a list page with loading, empty and error states.

weeks.title: Week 4: Real data: EF Core, SQL Server and routing
weeks.objective: Persist applications in SQL Server with EF Core migrations, and add detail pages with React Router.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Persistence + routing" merged: EF Core DbContext, migrations and seed data in SQL Server; React Router with list and detail pages.

weeks.title: Week 5: Search, filter, sort and paging
weeks.objective: Add server-side filtering, sorting and paging, and drive them from the URL with TanStack Query.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Search + paging" merged: query parameters with a paged response envelope; a filter bar that keeps state in the URL and caches pages with TanStack Query.

weeks.title: Week 6: Create and edit: validation on both sides
weeks.objective: Create and update applications with validation in the API and in the form, and keep the cache in sync after writes.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Create + edit" merged: POST/PUT with FluentValidation and ProblemDetails errors; React Hook Form + Zod forms with mutations and cache invalidation.

weeks.title: Week 7: Authentication: register and log in
weeks.objective: Add user accounts with ASP.NET Core Identity and JWT, and a login flow with protected routes in React.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Auth" merged: register/login endpoints issuing JWTs, every applications endpoint requires auth; React auth context, login page and protected routes.

weeks.title: Week 8: Authorization and sessions that last
weeks.objective: Enforce ownership and roles on the server, add refresh tokens, and handle expired sessions gracefully in the client.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Authorization + refresh" merged: policies and resource checks (403 vs 404), refresh-token rotation; client retries once on 401 and logs out cleanly.

weeks.title: Week 9: Interviews and notes: related data
weeks.objective: Model one-to-many relationships for interview rounds and notes, and build a tabbed detail page with optimistic updates.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Interviews + notes" merged: nested endpoints with EF relationships and cascade rules; detail page tabs with optimistic add and rollback.

weeks.title: Week 10: The Kanban board and concurrency
weeks.objective: Move applications between stages safely with concurrency control, through a drag-and-drop board.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Kanban" merged: PATCH status endpoint enforcing domain transitions with rowversion (409 on conflicts); dnd-kit board with optimistic moves and conflict handling.

weeks.title: Week 11: Tests that make changes safe
weeks.objective: Cover the API with real-database integration tests and the web app with component tests against a mocked API.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Tests" merged: WebApplicationFactory + Testcontainers SQL Server tests for auth and applications; Vitest + RTL + MSW tests for the main screens; both run with one command.

weeks.title: Week 12: Dashboard and performance
weeks.objective: Build an insights dashboard with efficient aggregate queries and keep the front end fast as it grows.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Dashboard" merged: stats endpoint with grouped queries, indexes and no N+1; dashboard with charts, memoisation where it helps, and route-level code splitting.

weeks.title: Week 13: Caching, rate limiting and fast search
weeks.objective: Cache safely on the server, protect the API from abuse, and make search feel instant in the client.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Caching + search" merged: output caching and Redis distributed cache with correct invalidation, rate limiting; debounced search with prefetching.

weeks.title: Week 14: Files and background jobs
weeks.objective: Attach resumes and offer letters to applications, and remind the user about follow-ups with scheduled background jobs.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Files + reminders" merged: validated file upload/download stored outside the database, Hangfire follow-up reminders; upload UI with progress and a reminders list.

weeks.title: Week 15: Real-time updates with SignalR
weeks.objective: Push reminders and status changes to open browsers in real time.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Real-time" merged: authenticated SignalR hub sending per-user events; React client that updates the cache and shows toasts, with reconnect handling.

weeks.title: Week 16: Resilience and observability
weeks.objective: Make failures survivable and visible: resilient outbound calls, structured logs and traces across the API, plus error boundaries in the UI.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Resilience + observability" merged: HttpClient resilience for an external company-info call, Serilog structured logs, OpenTelemetry traces; React error boundaries and client error reporting to the API.

weeks.title: Week 17: Events, messaging and the outbox
weeks.objective: Publish domain events reliably with the outbox pattern and RabbitMQ, and show an activity feed built from them.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Events" merged: domain events stored in an outbox and published to RabbitMQ, an idempotent consumer building activity entries and a weekly digest; activity feed page.

weeks.title: Week 18: Security hardening
weeks.objective: Harden both apps against the most common web and API attacks, and keep secrets out of the code.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Security" merged: OWASP API Top 10 review with fixes, secrets in user-secrets/Key Vault, security headers and strict CORS; client-side XSS review, CSP and dependency audit.

weeks.title: Week 19: Accessibility, UX polish and end-to-end tests
weeks.objective: Make the app usable by everyone on every screen size, and prove the main journeys work end to end.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Polish + E2E" merged: accessibility pass (keyboard, focus, contrast, labels), responsive layouts; Playwright tests for register → add application → move on board → add interview.

weeks.title: Week 20: Docker, CI/CD and deployment
weeks.objective: Containerise both apps, run the whole stack with one command, and deploy automatically from main.
weeks.deliverable: PR "Ship it" merged: Dockerfiles for API and web (nginx), docker compose with SQL Server, Redis and RabbitMQ; GitHub Actions building, testing and deploying both apps.

weeks.title: Week 21: Capstone: ready to show
weeks.objective: Turn JobHunt into a portfolio piece: documented architecture, a performance and quality pass, and a recorded walkthrough.
weeks.deliverable: Release v1.0: architecture diagram and decision records, README with screenshots and a live link, performance pass, and a 2-minute demo video.
